normalizations: frozen's #9618 case covers the same failed-helper session without the opt-in; this scenario adds PI_CLIPBOARD_OSC52=1, which is what turns the failure into a written sequence

upstreamTest.case: PI_CLIPBOARD_OSC52=1 emits OSC 52 after a successful linux copy

scenarios.name: osc52-opt-in-writes-the-largest-allowed-payload-in-full
normalizations: the 75000-byte payload's sequence is recorded by encodedLengths plus its exact heads/tails, not in full

frozen has no at-the-bound case; its only size case is the over-bound rejection (clipboard.test.ts:317), so this scenario has no upstreamTest and asserts the largest accepted payload against MAX_OSC52_ENCODED_LENGTH

scenarios.name: osc52-opt-in-rejects-one-byte-over-the-size-bound

outcome.error: Clipboard unavailable: text exceeds the OSC 52 size limit

normalizations: the 75001-byte payload is refused, so the observation is the failure message
frozen's case uses an 80000-byte payload in an SSH remote session; this scenario stays one byte over the bound and reaches it through the opt-in instead

upstreamTest.case: does not emit oversized OSC 52 payloads

scenarios.name: wsl-windows-terminal-prefers-osc52-before-the-remote-branch
normalizations: frozen's case covers the WSL/Windows-Terminal preference without the opt-in or DISPLAY; this scenario adds DISPLAY=:0 with a failing xclip, then PI_CLIPBOARD_OSC52=1, to observe that the later remote branch does not write a second sequence

upstreamTest.case: WSL in Windows Terminal prefers OSC 52 over PowerShell
